Measured, but not enough to determine the curve — one geometry, or several that are linearly dependent (two resolutions of one area; several frame counts at one area). The peak is known AT those geometries and the slopes are undeterminable, so nothing is known about the rest of the envelope.

Measured geometries of full design rank — sufficient to determine the affine curve, which is not a claim that a fit has been performed. `coveredPixelBound` is the largest measured area; `coveredFrameBound`, present only on cells carrying a temporal geometry, is the largest measured frame count.

summary.publicationPredicate: A coordinate is published when it is PLANNED (an entry in config/memory-calibration-plan.json targets it), MEASURED (memoryCharacterization is not `unmeasured`), BOUND to a calibration record in docs/generated/memory-calibration-evidence.json, or CITES evidence of its own (historical, current-environment, strategy-parameter, or structural). Every elided coordinate is therefore unplanned, unmeasured, unbound and uncited; its `state` and its per-rung population are counted in `summary.elidedByState` and `coverage`, never dropped.

Component scope and streamability are two different levers and must not be conflated. Making the encoder streamable at all under Sequential is what let bf16 fit 8 GB (conditioning 8.489 -> 2.718 GiB); the tunable TextEncoder scope cuts conditioning a further 46.5% and moves the request peak 0.0%, which is why the published default is Dit — see gen-core's memory_strategy prerequisite note.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The pinned provider now exposes two distinct measured Lens identities. Base `lens` Q4 uses the full shared ladder and rebuilds both the 24-layer gpt-oss encoder and 48-block DiT with window 1. `lens_turbo` BF16 retains the earlier text-encoder-only window-1 contract. The entry/tier cross-products, adapters, PiD, eager loads, and other numeric tiers remain outside both contracts.
findings: The gpt-oss encoder is MoE. A window over its layers materializes ALL experts of each layer in the window, not the top-k a token routes to, so the per-block cost of a TE-scoped window is the full expert set — a parameter-sizing consequence, not a blocker.

Dense BF16 conditioning scales with the resident window: 80.098 GiB at 24 layers, 33.136 at 8, 21.271 at 4, 15.340 at 2, and 8.767 at 1. Exact identity held at windows 1, 4, and 24; replacing the 24-layer stack with zero layers changed the output by 1.2079592e4, proving the bound is load-bearing.

Lens does not pad every prompt to one fixed token length. Its harmony preamble is fixed, but the measured prompts produced 121, 141, and 181 tokens; window=1 conditioning peaks were 8.748, 8.767, and 8.807 GiB respectively.

The Q4 result is entry-specific: base `lens` Q4 now has a measured full-ladder request win, while `lens_turbo` Q4's text-encoder-only experiment reproducibly increased the full-request peak and remains Missing.

Adapter cells remain Missing, not Structurally N/A. The provider also rejects PiD for this measured contract, although PiD is a request option rather than an overlay axis in this matrix. The TextEncoder primitive is not inherently incapable of coexisting with either; separate dynamic evidence would be required before broadening the production predicate.

The declaration is per load and the matrix has no load-source or materialization axis. The worker opts only base Lens Q4 and Lens-Turbo BF16 directory routes into deferred materialization; a single-file, eager, or Resident load does not receive either contract.

A second, independent gpt-oss stack exists: `LensReasonerModel.layers` (24) sits OUTSIDE the Sequential seam, which only knows the text and heavy bundles, so nothing on this ladder sheds it. It is LATENT rather than live: `attach_reasoner` has no production callers and the registry path leaves it off, so no catalog route reaches it today. It matters only if a route ever turns it on.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The FLUX MMDiT skeleton with pruned adaLN — 19 double + 38 single uniform sub-stacks windowed through `mlx_gen::block_residency::run_windowed`, plus a small distribution approximator that feeds every block's modulation and stays resident. All three catalog entries are the same provider route (one architecture, one loader, one contract shape), differing only in checkpoint, sampler default and schedule; every measured number is Chroma1-Base's own, never inherited from FLUX.1 or a sibling.
findings: Pruned adaLN makes this family MORE window-friendly than stock FLUX, not less: the blocks carry no `.norm*.linear` weights and take their modulation as a slice of one approximator output computed once per step. That output is a small resident tensor, and the per-block weight bytes a window must materialize are correspondingly smaller.

Rung 2 is `Missing` on an UNRESOLVED margin, not a clean failure. Tiling the FLUX.1 16-ch VAE decode works and the saving is large (−11.4% to −72.4% of the decode phase across 28 swept geometries at the variant's real 28-step schedule), but the best cell (edge 832 / overlap 256) drifts 53/255 against the 48/255 bar the closest sibling admits — and resampling that one geometry across five production latents gives max-drift 28..82, a 2.9× spread that straddles the bar. Nothing in that supports admission, and calling it a clean rejection would overstate the evidence; resolving it needs a quality methodology (perceptual metric or a family-derived bar) the epic has not agreed on.

Rung 3 is `Missing` on a measured verdict: `sdpa_budgeted_bhsd` reaches both block stacks and both attention sites and saves −2.27% at the DiT seam (7.1679 → 7.0053 GiB, bit-exact), but the seam sits ~12 GiB inside the staged request peak so the REQUEST moves −0.001% — which per the epic is not a saving. MLX's fused SDPA streams its scores (no materialized [B,H,Sq,Sk] to bound), and Chroma's MMDiT mask is a per-query [B,1,S,S] tensor (85 MiB per CFG branch at 1024²) the bounded kernel must narrow per chunk.

The rung-4 scope default is `Dit`, and it is measured rather than inherited — the naive phase probe predicts the opposite. T5-XXL is the largest single component (dense bf16 at 10.15 GiB against a 7.14 GiB packed DiT), which makes `TextEncoder` look obviously right; but rung 1 has already shed it before the heavy phase loads, so a `TextEncoder` window moves the request peak −0.00%. The verdict is coupled to rung 2's: a bounded decode would drop the heavy phase below conditioning and flip the binding scope (Kolors/SC-15521 is the same arithmetic with a different decode).

The cadence domain [1, 2, 5, 10] is published as equal-peak alternatives, not a latency frontier: all four bound the request to 14.6932 GiB, and the ms/step ordering moves with execution-order slots and is unresolvable on this instrument (sc-17679). The default 1 rests on being the tightest weight bound.

findings: See the SDXL family entry (SC-15525) for why a U-Net is not Structurally N/A here. Kolors inherits that verdict exactly, because it inherits the module — but it inherits NONE of the numbers, because it conditions on ChatGLM3-6B rather than SDXL's CLIP-L + OpenCLIP-bigG pair, and that inverts which phase carries the request peak at several advertised geometries.

Kolors is the first family in the ladder to publish a rung-4 SCOPE domain of more than one value: `transformer_window_components = [Dit, TextEncoder, Both]`. The matrix already carries the scope axis as `transformerWindowComponent` inside `strategyParameters` (and `transformerWindowComponents` inside `publishedRanges`), so no schema change was needed to express it — but this is the first time the domain is genuinely three-valued and the choice is load-bearing rather than degenerate.

The production default stays the TIGHT cadence 1, unlike SDXL's 10, and the `Dit` scope, unlike the `Both` that wins at 512². Both are the provider's declarations; the selector may name any point in the published domains.

Rungs 2 and 3 are `Missing` WITH measurements. Rung 2 is by a wide margin the biggest lever on this family's ladder — at 1024² q4 it takes the whole staged request from 16.0412 → 9.9981 GiB (−37.67%) for +10% wall clock (925 → 1018 ms/step), against rung 4's −7.21% for +4.2× — and it CLEARS the 48/255 inherited drift bar at 1024² (38) and 1280² (26), but FAILS it at 1536² (69) and 2048² (53). `MemoryParameterRanges::decode_tile_edges` is an absolute pixel domain with no geometry axis, so no fixed edge holds a constant tile fraction across a 2× output range; the unlock is tracked as sc-17678. Rung 3 moves the peak 0.00% at both measured scopes — the request (16.0412 → 16.0410 GiB) and the U-Net seam (5.3652 → 5.3652 GiB, reproduced across three runs) — and is not bit-exact (max|Δeps| 3.929e-3, 16/255 of image movement at one step, 212/255 by four). An earlier revision published the seam as +12.54% from an un-warmed control: MLX's first `run` in a process reads ~4.6-4.8 GiB whichever plan it executes.

findings: The story's first trap is confirmed against the code and the classification is `partial`, not N/A. Its `[0, 2, 10]` shorthand is right about the SHAPE: the config array is [1, 2, 10], but level 0 is a DownBlock2D/UpBlock2D with no attention, so its entry is never read and the effective depths are 2 and 10.

SC-15525's survey text said SDXL has FOUR 2-deep `Transformer2D` sub-stacks. It is FIVE: the down path contributes two (down_blocks.1) and the up path three, because an up block carries `layers_per_block + 1 = 3` attentions. The full forward-order depth array is [2, 2, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 2, 2, 2] — eleven Transformer2D, 70 windowable blocks.

The skip connections bound the SIZE of the win, not its validity. They keep down-path ACTIVATIONS alive across the forward, and rung 4 bounds WEIGHT residency — so the weight bound over each 10-deep sub-stack still holds; what does not shrink is the activation term it is competing against. The measured wins (−6.97% to −21.40% by tier) are that competition priced.

The rung needs a plan PER Transformer2D, not one per model, and that is what shipped: eleven `BlockPlan`s at a shared cadence. `BlockPlan::new` clamps a window to its stack's depth, so a cadence wider than 2 degrades the five 2-deep sub-stacks to fully resident rather than erroring — which is why the domain is stated once and not per depth, and why 10 is the widest cadence that means anything here.

Rungs 2 and 3 are `Missing` WITH measurements rather than unattempted. Rung 2's tiled decode works and is the family's biggest lever — 19.0032 → 15.8660 GiB (−16.51%) of request peak for ~7% wall clock, isolated decode 14.360 → 11.237 GiB (−21.7%) at edge 896 — but it is withheld on QUALITY: the inherited sibling drift bar is 48/255, and on the production latent the same 1024²/edge-896/overlap-192 geometry drifts 84/255 (the synthetic-latent sweep read 38, which is why the withholding argument had to be measured on production latents). It fails the bar outright at 1280²/1536²/2048², and `decode_tile_edges` has no geometry axis to vary the edge with output size. Rung 3's `sdpa_budgeted_bhsd` reaches every attention site including the IP-Adapter branch, but moves the peak 0.00% at BOTH measured scopes — the request (19.0032 → 19.0032 GiB) and the U-Net seam (6.5868 → 6.5868 GiB) — and is not bit-exact on its query-row axis (max|Δeps| 5.25e-3 at one step; 57/255 of image movement at one step, a different image by six). An earlier revision published the seam as +5.1% from an un-warmed control; warmed, both U-Nets read +0.00%.

illustrious_xl_v1 and illustrious_xl_v2 are `Missing` at rung 4 outright, because q8 is their only advertised tier. The cause is the SNAPSHOT, not the architecture: their `unet/` weights are genuinely packed (u32 codes with .scales/.biases, 3.46 GiB, byte-for-byte realvisxl q8's shape) but their `unet/config.json` ships without the `quantization` marker, so `packed_quant_bits` reads nothing, `needs_load_time_quant` returns true, `load_leaves_blocks_lazy` is false and `streamable` refuses. The rung fails closed, which is correct; the repair is a republished snapshot, tracked as sc-17522.

The remaining q4/q8 reconciliation overclaims are the committed capability dump under-reporting: `streamable` is tier-agnostic on a packed snapshot, but the dump enumerates surfaces with a synthetic weights-free LoadSpec, so `load_leaves_blocks_lazy` fails closed at q4/q8. rung4SurveyRows.summary: The Candle renderer also switches between two uniform Wan expert stacks during denoise. It publishes no sequential-offload or block-window contract, so the two-stack opportunity is in scope but unimplemented.

The two 40-block experts and mode-independent renderer make rung 4 structurally applicable on every image/video mode, but structural opportunity, provider implementation, and measured request saving remain three separate facts.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: Two uniform 40-block Wan expert stacks form one 80-block global window space. Both experts load deferred and mlx-gen's shared block-residency runner materializes only the selected window, so the old finding that an idle expert remains resident is no longer true.
findings: Rung 0 is the no-extra-controls baseline: both experts co-reside during denoise. Rung 2 is a real request-selected spatial tile edge over `[768, 640, 512, 384, 320, 256]` with overlap 64; rung 3 is a request-selected attention budget over both experts; rung 4 is a request-selected global 80-block deferred stream with windows `[1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20]` and default 10. The same phase and trunk mechanisms serve every video mode (`t2v`, `v2v`, `r2v`, `rv2v`, `mv2v`, `ads2v`) and the one-frame image entry. Modes change conditioning inputs and guidance pass count, not the stage order or decoder. Guided modes re-walk a window several times per denoise step, which is a latency cost rather than a different applicability verdict.

No image cell is assigned a modality-specific value by this reconciliation: `bernini_image` and `bernini` intentionally share this one provider verdict. The generated-artifact review must still diff image cells after the final inference pin; a pin-derived state change is not to be hidden by falsifying the shared survey.

sc-21609 (Michael's coverage decision): the Mlx bernini RULES row now exists with legacy_shaping:true, so MLX bernini loads are shaped to DeferredMaterialization and the engine's rung 4 is reachable — plain loads stream, adapted (Wan-adapter) loads stay off the stream at the engine's own `structurally_streamable` gate. Two residues stay recorded rather than resolved: the route registry's mode vocabulary is image-only, so the video-mode coordinates (t2v/v2v/r2v/rv2v/mv2v/ads2v) can never carry a witness even though the shaping fires for them (the MLX consult site passes text_to_image for every cold load) — the reconciliation reads them as wildcard-expanded, not as drift; and the request-peak measurement for this family remains absent, so implementation is still not evidence of a measured request-level saving.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: One uniform 40-block causal Wan transformer. Its per-layer causal KV cache changes carried state and latency, but not the fact that the weight trunk is one sequential stack; no block-window materializer is wired.
findings: Rung 1 is unconditional, not selectable: the corrected tuple is `(false, true)` for all t2v/i2v/v2v paths. Rung 2 is automatic budgeted z16 decode. The causal KV history window bounds temporal attention context as part of model execution, but it is not the shared request-selected BoundedAttention strategy and must not promote rung 3. Rung 4 is Missing.

The family has no quant-tier axis in this survey claim beyond what the manifest actually hosts; no tier-conditioned applicability or request-peak result is invented. Candle is recorded once under `unroutedBackends`, not as five Missing rungs.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The same uniform 48-block AvDiT. LTX-2.5's adapter-free BF16/Q4 split route drives the shared block-window primitive; Q8 remains unadvertised pending SC-18783 evidence. Its ordinary ConvVAE route also consumes a selected decode edge/overlap, while the optional DiffVAE route and staged residency remain Missing for those respective controls. LTX-2.3 and every adapter-bearing coordinate, including LTX-2.5 dev's required refinement adapter, remain outside the rung-4 implementation scope.
findings: **The Candle rung-1 question, answered: the Gemma text encoder is RESIDENT, not staged.** The encoder is a field of `Components` (`lib.rs:79-80`), the bundle is built once and stored in `Mutex<Option<Components>>` (`:367`) by `candle_gen::cached` (`:374-376`), and `candle-gen/src/sync.rs:52-58` stores on miss and never clears — so the encoder outlives the request, not merely the encode. `load_components` builds the AvDiT FIRST and the encoder SECOND with no free between (`:168-174`; same order on the packed-tier path at `:227-236`), so the two co-reside from the first load onward. `render` takes `comps: &Components` (`:276`), which means it structurally CANNOT drop it: the encode at `:284-285` is followed by the denoise at `:303`/`:316` with `comps.te` still alive. Greps over the crate for `drop(`, `clear_cache`, `unload`, `release`, `empty_cache`, `Drop for` and `residency` find no free path. The fit gate agrees from the other direction: `component_footprint` (`:645-654`) sizes `text_encoder` and `dit` as a partition of ONE simultaneous load, documented at `:619-623` as "the slots are a partition of the load".

The residency result remains the inverse of the MLX twin: `resident` is the Candle baseline and `staged_residency` is a real Missing, whereas MLX stages its text encoder unconditionally. LTX-2.5's Candle contract deliberately declares no staged-residency prerequisite for its device-format block transfer, so its adapter-free rung-4 cells remain Implemented/unverified even while rung 1 is Missing; the two states are independent rather than a reason to copy MLX staging onto Candle.

What is held alongside the trunk during denoise is what most limits rung 4's reach on this backend: `Components` keeps the ~24 GB Gemma encoder, the video VAE and the audio decoder + vocoder alive through the whole block loop (`lib.rs:79-97`), none of which is needed until after it. Rung 4 bounds the 48 blocks; on Candle it cannot bound the majority of what is resident while they run. Not inventoried in `blockStacks` because none of it is transformer trunk weight — recorded here per this survey's own convention for encoder and decode-side residents.

LTX-2.3's budgeted VAE decode remains its existing automatic path. LTX-2.5 independently wires the selected edge/overlap through `selected_decode_cap` into the ConvVAE's `decode_budgeted_with_spatial_cap`; its optional DiffVAE retains an automatic chunked route and explicitly rejects those parameters. The static declaration therefore describes the ordinary ConvVAE load, not a claim that the alternate decoder accepts the same control.

LTX-2.3 retains its existing fixed attention guard. LTX-2.5 separately publishes selectable score-element budgets [67108864,16777216] on its ordinary attention path, so the implemented declaration is provider- and entry-specific rather than a family inference.

Rung 4 remains absent for LTX-2.3. LTX-2.5's BF16/Q4 split route instead drives gen_core::block_window over the 48-block AvDiT for deferred, directory-backed, adapter-free loads, with published windows [1,2,4,8,16]. Candle Q8 remains outside the registered memory surface pending SC-18783 evidence.

Candle adapters are forward-time residuals, but the shipped LTX-2.5 block stream refuses adapter-bearing loads rather than replaying them per window. Its rung-4 scope is therefore no-overlay only, including exclusion of the dev transformer's required refinement adapter.

On the DISTILLED LoRA specifically: there is no fold to undo on this backend because `ltx_2_3_eros` no longer routes to Candle (sc-18902). Exact-head CUDA baseline run 31766800005 proved that sending its undistilled dense checkpoint through Candle's single distilled denoise pass produces unresolved noise with no prompt subject. The published cond_safe recipe cannot be transferred honestly: it is two-pass on MLX and only 768/3,320 keys match Candle's narrower adapter surface (`transformer_blocks.N.attn{1,2}.{to_q,to_k,to_v,to_out.0}` only, `adapters.rs:49-60`). Base LTX and its user LoRAs remain compatible with the Candle forward-time residual mechanism described above.

SC-18902 keeps `ltx_2_3_eros` MLX-only after its failed Candle baseline. The new Candle rung-4 claim is not a resurrection of that route: it is scoped solely to `ltx_2_5`, and only to the adapter-free split-provider coordinates named above.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: One uniform 48-block AvDiT stack walked by a single loop; only the per-modality patchify/adaLN embedders and the two output heads sit outside it. LTX-2.5's adapter-free distilled route drives the shared block-window primitive over that stack. LTX-2.3, Eros, user-LoRA coordinates, and LTX-2.5 dev's mandatory stage-two refinement adapter remain outside the implementation scope.
findings: Rung 1 is engaged UNCONDITIONALLY, and this is the one place in the family where the capability flag and the behaviour disagree. `stage_text_phase` (`model.rs:578`) builds the Gemma TE, runs prompt enhancement and `encode_av` inside one scope (`:579-585`), then forces the graph with `mlx_rs::transforms::eval` (`:588`) so lazy evaluation cannot keep the ~24 GB of weights alive past the scope, and lets `te` drop at end of scope; the caller `mlx_rs::memory::clear_cache()`s immediately after (`:1186`) and only then builds the AvDiT (`:759`, comment `:756-758`: "so the TE and the DiT never co-reside"). So `supports_sequential_offload: false` (`:269-270`) UNDER-reports on this backend: the staging ships, it is simply not driven by the shared `Residency` seam. sc-18816 owns making that visible to the ladder; this verdict describes the behaviour as it is at the pinned revision.

`resident` is NOT a reachable state for MLX LTX, and should not be scored as if it were selectable. No code path co-resides the TE and the AvDiT, so the family's floor is already `max(TE, DiT)` rather than their sum and a `resident` measurement would have nothing to measure. sc-18808's real-weight capture corroborates it from the allocator side at 768x512x97 q8: `stagedTextEncoderBytes` 32.73 GB and `stagedTransformerBytes` 20.61 GB against a `costagedGiantsBytes` bound of 53.35 GB, with active memory dropping from `denoiseEntryActive` 20.69 GB to `decodeEntryActive` 1.02 GB.

The AvDiT is staged too, not only the text encoder: `model.rs:806-808` `eval`s the latents, `drop(transformer)`s and `clear_cache()`s before `decode_to_frames` (`:811`). That is what makes the 48-block trunk essentially the entire denoise-phase residency and gives rung 4 a larger share to move here than on any image family — but it is also why the request-peak question below is not answered by the trunk's size.

Where the request peak actually sits, from the one real-weight capture — and it is not the trunk. At 768x512x97 q8 (`ltx-2-3-mlx-q8-768x512-f97-fps24-seed18808`) the phase active peaks are `conditioningActivePeak` 35.56 GB, `denoiseActivePeak` 27.44 GB, `decodeActivePeak` 15.03 GB: the request peak is the CONDITIONING phase, i.e. the text encoder that rung 1 already stages, not the denoise trunk that rung 4 would bound. At that geometry a perfect rung-4 window could not move the request peak at all. This is n=1, one tier, one geometry, and video activations grow with frames as well as area, so denoise may well dominate at the top of the envelope (1280x704, 449 frames) — which is exactly why the finding here is `unmeasured` and not `does-not-move`. It does mean a rung-4 measurement for this family has to be taken across the frames axis, not at one geometry.

Rung 2 ships and auto-selects, but is INERT at the geometries this host renders. `decode_to_frames` (`pipeline.rs:157`) calls `auto_tiling_budgeted_ltx(out_h, out_w, out_f)` (`:260`) and tiles only when the modelled peak exceeds 85% of `get_memory_limit()` (`:266-267`); the shared planner returns `Ok(None)` when a single pass fits under the budget and the frame count is under the i32 write cap (`crates/contracts/gen-core/src/tiling.rs:840-843`). The cost model (`pipeline.rs:239-255`) puts 768x512x97 at ~15.15 GiB against an ~103 GiB budget on the sc-18808 host (`mlxMemoryLimitBytes` 130.6 GB x 0.85), so decode is single-pass there and rung 2 is implemented-but-not-engaged. Implemented is not engaged, and the matrix must not read the two as the same claim.

Rung 3 remains Missing on LTX-2.3, whose only candidate is the training-only `ckpt_sdpa` recomputation path. LTX-2.5 is different: its provider contract publishes [67108864,16777216] score-element budgets and its ordinary attention path consumes the selected budget. The implementation claim is therefore entry-scoped, never copied back to 2.3 or Eros.

LTX adapters remain forward-time residuals, but the shipped 2.5 block stream deliberately refuses every adapter-bearing load because it does not replay those residuals during block re-materialization. The implementation scope is consequently `overlays: ["none"]`; mechanism-level compatibility is not used to authorize a route the loader rejects.

On the DISTILLED LoRA specifically — the overlay this family was asked about, and it is a LIVE RUNTIME overlay on this backend, not a baked one. `ltx_2_3_eros` declares `mlx.autoDistillLora` (`config/manifests/builtin.models.jsonc:11174`) and ships the cond_safe distill LoRA as a `coRequisite` download (`:11087-11098`) because its base checkpoint is NOT pre-distilled — without it the MLX video collapses to noise a few frames in (`crates/sceneworks-worker/src/video_jobs/ltx.rs:738-742`). The worker injects it AHEAD of the user LoRAs as an `AdapterSpec` carrying `pass_scales = [stage1, stage2]` (`ltx.rs:693-703`, resolver `:754`, MLX-gated at `:753`). Base `ltx_2_3` declares none and injects nothing (`crates/sceneworks-worker/src/video_jobs/tests.rs:10224`), because its hosted tiers are assembled FROM the distilled checkpoint at conversion time (`builtin.models.jsonc:10966`) — so the family carries both shapes at once, one baked and one injected.

LTX-2.5 dev requires the bundled stage-two refinement LoRA with pass scales [0,1]. That makes its LoadSpec adapter-bearing and therefore non-streamable under the provider's exact predicate. The adapter-free scope above describes the already-refined distilled transformer only; it must not be read as dev authority or as a promise to replay user adapters.

One second network is held resident and invoked MID-denoise, between the two passes: `LatentUpsampler` (`upsampler.rs:179`), called at `pipeline.rs:967` and again on the IC-LoRA path at `:1094` while the AvDiT is still live. It is deliberately NOT inventoried in `blockStacks`: it is a conv/ResBlock latent upscaler loaded from its own checkpoint, not transformer trunk weight, and `model.rs:312` records the intent — "The small components (each << the TE / DiT) stay resident". It is recorded here because a rung-4 window schedule for this family has to survive being re-entered for a second pass over an upscaled latent, which no image family's plan has to do.

The family now has three catalog entries with one 48-block AvDiT shape and different artifact/loader contracts. `ltx_2_3` and `ltx_2_3_eros` retain their prior Missing rung-4 verdicts. Only `ltx_2_5`'s q4/q8/bf16 adapter-free cells are implemented, which is why the declaration is an implementationScope rather than a family-wide claim.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The distinct Candle SCAIL-2 engine carries the same uniform 40-block trunk, but caches one resident Components bundle and has no block-window loader.
findings: Rung 0 is resident. Rung 1 is Missing `(false, false)`: the cached Components bundle outlives each request. Rung 2 is Missing on the actual route because it calls plain decode. Rung 3 uses fixed provider-local budgeted SDPA, not a shared request selection. Rung 4 is Missing.

This lane was absent only from the old JavaScript route parser. SC-18828 repairs the oracle by following the canonical backend-existence predicate's direct model-id slice and pins `scail2_14b:candle` in regression tests.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: One homogeneous 40-block Wan2.1-14B I2V stack. The architecture fits one block plan, but the shipped SCAIL-2 provider eagerly owns all blocks and exposes no block-window path.
findings: Rung 1 is unconditional rather than selectable: the corrected tuple is `(false, true)`. UMT5 and CLIP are loaded, evaluated and freed before DiT execution, but there is no shared request resolver. Rung 2 is automatic budgeted z16 decode. Rung 3 has optional provider-local query/FFN chunk controls, but the shipped default/request surface does not declare the shared selectable BoundedAttention strategy. Rung 4 is Missing.
The model is macOS-download-only in the manifest. That distribution fact does not erase the distinct Candle runtime route below and does not justify an MLX-only family verdict.

Selectable phase residency and bounded decode/attention do not supply the missing multi-stack block-window implementation.

convolutional / ResNet U-Net trunk and skip path

findings: Rung 0 is resident and rung 1 is selectable `(true, false)`: the shared lifecycle runs conditioner → U-Net → decoder with synchronized release. Rung 2 combines request-selected temporal chunks with automatic spatial budget tiling. Rung 3 uses provider-local budgeted attention. Rung 4 is Missing, not Structurally N/A: the 32 one-block nested transformer stacks are a real partial opportunity, but Candle has no materializer or scheduling plan spanning them.

Its heterogeneous convolutional U-Net contains 16 separately indexed TransformerSpatioTemporal modules: six in the cross-attention down stages, one in the mid stage, and nine in the cross-attention up stages. Every module owns one spatial BasicBlock and one TemporalBlock, while the surrounding ResNet/conv/skip trunk is non-windowable, so the exact survey verdict is partial.

nested temporal transformer stacks across down / mid / up attention modules

findings: Rung 0 is resident and rung 1 is Missing `(false, false)`. Rung 2 exposes temporal decode chunking but no Candle-style automatic spatial budget planner at this pin. Rung 3 uses the ordinary fused attention path with no bounded request control. Rung 4 is Missing, not Structurally N/A: the 32 one-block nested transformer stacks make the architecture partially applicable, but no MLX materializer or scheduling plan spans them.
SVD is dual-lane and untiered. Neither fact permits a tier-conditioned claim, and the MLX verdict must not be erased merely because the filed story described only Candle i2v.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: TI2V-5B is a single 30-block trunk and A14B is a dual 40-block MoE; VACE modes add a separate control path. All are eager Candle loads and none exposes a block-window loader. VACE-Fun is not routed on Candle and is not silently included in this backend verdict.
findings: Rung 1 is selectable for the 5B and A14B providers, `(true, false)`, but absent for Candle Wan-VACE, `(false, false)`. Rung 2 is implemented for the ordinary Wan routes by the reviewed decode contract and provider VAE tilers. Rung 3 has fixed provider-local budgeted SDPA but no request-selected contract. Rung 4 is Missing everywhere.

The reviewed TI2V-5B contract applies only to `wan2_2_ti2v_5b`, directory-backed native bf16/packed loads. It explicitly declines a calibrated contract for native GGUF and does not cover T2V-A14B, I2V-A14B, or Wan-VACE. Planned GGUF expert swapping therefore contributes no implemented rung at this pin.
No Candle verdict is emitted for `wan_2_2_vace_fun_14b`: SceneWorks' new routing row is MLX-only and the worker rejects the absent Candle provider rather than substituting another Wan engine.

rung4SurveyRows.summary: The family is deliberately partial rather than rounded: TI2V-5B is one uniform 30-block trunk, while the A14B T2V/I2V and VACE-Fun entries are dual 40-block experts; VACE-Fun adds per-expert VACE modules. No Wan catalog route drives a block-window implementation at the surveyed heads.
findings: Rung 0 remains the provider baseline. Rung 1 is physically engaged on every MLX Wan route, but the shared-seam bit is entry-specific: TI2V-5B, T2V-A14B, I2V-A14B and VACE-Fun are `(supports_sequential_offload, unconditionally_engages_staged_residency) = (true, true)`; the single-expert `wan_vace` provider reached through advanced modes is `(false, true)`. These are not interchangeable claims: `false` means no shared selectable seam, while the unconditional phase drops are still real.

Rung 2 is implemented by the provider-owned z48/z16 budgeted decode paths. Engagement depends on geometry and memory budget; an untiled fit is not evidence that the mechanism is absent. Rung 3 has real provider-local attention budgeting in the Wan transformer, but the pending TI2V-5B contract correctly leaves the shared request-selected BoundedAttention strategy Missing. Rung 4 is Missing for every entry: no ordinary Wan load constructs the deferred block stream Bernini uses.

The pending MLX TI2V-5B provider contract is narrower than this family: it declares Resident and BoundedDecode Implemented, while StagedResidency, BoundedAttention and BoundedTransformerResidency remain Missing as request-selected strategies. It must not be copied onto either A14B expert or VACE. Physical unconditional staging is carried by the separate descriptor flag, not invented as a selectable contract.

`wan_2_2_vace_fun_14b` was a catalog defect, not a deliberately unavailable model.
